citation-1.title: Geographically Weighted Regression: A Method for Exploring Spatial Nonstationarity
citation-1.abstract: Geographically weighted regression (GWR) is a technique for modeling spatially varying relationships between variables. It is designed to produce a more localized understanding of spatial nonstationarity. This paper presents an overview of the GWR methodology and discusses its application in various fields such as geography and environmental science.

citation-2.title: Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR)
citation-2.abstract: Multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) is a new mapping method that enables the estimation of multi-scale relationships between independent and dependent variables across geographic space. MGWR extends the ideas of geographically weighted regression (GWR) in two dimensions to account for the presence of local variations in the scale of the identified relationships. The methodological basis of MGWR is provided, including the estimation of local scale parameters using a local metric for model fitting. The application of MGWR is illustrated using a dataset of housing prices in remote areas of a major city, offering insights into the importance of scale in real estate markets. Finally, the potential for further methodological developments is discussed.

citation-3.title: NewsViews: an automated pipeline for creating custom geovisualizations for news
citation-3.abstract: The increasing complexity of news data necessitates new ways to conceptualize and visualize information beyond simple text. In this paper, we present NewsViews, a novel automated pipeline that enables users to create custom geovisualizations of news articles. We illustrate how NewsViews transforms unstructured data into interactive visual representations that support exploration and understanding of the underlying stories. Our approach leverages both geographic and semantic analysis to generate astute visual summaries, allowing users to engage with the data dynamically. We also discuss the implications for designing effective geovisualizations that serve the diverse needs of the news audience.

citation-4.title: Visualizing Multiple Variables Across Scale and Geography
citation-4.abstract: This paper presents a framework for visualizing multiple variables across scale and geography. We propose techniques to handle both large datasets and scaling phenomena in a coherent manner. Our approach leverages multiscale representations to provide insights into spatial and temporal patterns, supporting users in their exploration and understanding of complex data.

reference_mentions: Support for a variety of spatial models is integrated into the most widely used geographic information systems (GIS). However, these systems and notebooks do not support integrated external knowledge sources to help contextualize models [6]. They also require analysts to judiciously choose the proper tools at every stage of the analytical pipeline to build a well-trained model. This process necessitates a solid foundation in geographical concepts and can be time-consuming, even for seasoned analysts. Our goal is to enhance the spatial modeling process through a deliberately designed userfriendly workflow and automatically generated explanatory narratives guided by domain experts to promote the understanding of local contextual information from models. Our work focuses on improving model explainability, enabling interactive report authoring, and supporting contextualization through narrative generation. This is important in local models such as GWR and MGWR because the main output from such models is a set of local parameter estimates from each process being modeled, and the spatial variation in these estimates needs to be explained in terms of the contextualized environment of each location by providing additional contextual information for users.

citation-8.title: Interacting with Predictions: Visual Inspection of Black-box Machine Learning Models
citation-8.abstract: Black-box machine learning models are being applied to a wide range of tasks including image recognition, natural language processing, and medical diagnosis, often in high-stakes scenarios where the consequences of errors can be severe. However, the lack of interpretability of these models makes it difficult for users to understand their behaviors. In this paper, we present a novel approach that provides users with the ability to inspect and interact with predictions made by black-box models. Our system enables users to visually explore important features driving predictions, allowing for a more informed understanding of model outputs. We demonstrate the capabilities of our approach through case studies and user evaluations, discussing implications for practice and future research.

citation-12.title: The State‐of‐the‐Art in Predictive Visual Analytics
citation-12.abstract: Predictive visual analytics is an emerging field that combines predictive modeling with interactive visualization to support data-driven decision-making. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art techniques and applications in predictive visual analytics. We categorize existing methods into three main areas: (1) visual exploration of predictive models, (2) visual interpretation of model outputs, and (3) visual design of predictive models. For each area, we discuss representative techniques, highlight their strengths and limitations, and identify open challenges. We also present a taxonomy of predictive visual analytics tasks and provide an overview of existing tools and systems. Finally, we discuss future research directions and potential applications of predictive visual analytics in various domains.

citation-14.title: A Partition-Based Framework for Building and Validating Regression Models
citation-14.abstract: Regression models play a crucial role in data analysis, enabling users to understand relationships in data sets as well as to make predictions. This paper introduces a general approach for building and validating regression models based on multivariate partitioning. We present a unified framework that encompasses various types of regression models, including linear regression and more complex models with interactions of predictors. A key focus is on using the partitioning structure to improve interpretability and validation of the resulting models. By providing an overview of the advantages and challenges of different model types, we allow users to make informed choices about model selection and validation. Additionally, our framework includes novel methods for visualizing the results of regression analyses in an intuitive manner, thus catering to a diverse audience ranging from statisticians to data scientists and domain experts.

reference_mentions: Most closely related to our work are the techniques that explain models from feature-level observation. Muhlbacher and ¨ Piringer [14] facilitated feature selection and optimization in regression models by partitioning the feature space into disjoint regions for visualization. Sedlmair et al. [17] proposed an abstract conceptual framework to discuss the visual parameter space analysis problems independent of the application domain. Goodwin et al. [4] extended visual parameter space analysis to the spatial domain, enabling the exploration of correlations between multiple variables that vary geographically at different spatial scales. While these techniques focus on explanations for domain experts, our work is designed to support explanations to experts and support their use of external information to contextualize these relationships and communicate their findings to a general audience. Our choice of text templates, as opposed to large language models, for narrative generation is to support control for reliability and reproducibility. All text generated must have a verifiable source and the generation of text for the analysis should always return the same results to ensure that the resulting analyses are not subject to misinformation.

citation-25.abstract: EnsembleMatrix is an interactive visualization tool that supports the use of multiple classifiers in machine learning. reference_mentions: Narrative visualization is directly related to the concept of explainability, where the visualization authors seek to couple images and text to explain an underlying data analysis. With respect to model explainability, the visual analytics community has developed a variety of systems to support the interactive explanation of machine learning models (e.g. [22, 12]). Several model-independent approaches, e.g. EnsembleMatrix [25] and RuleMatrix [13], focus on the classifier's input-output behaviors to provide insight into the model classification results.
